Ok, not a funny comment but here me out. It's false that true communism has never been tried: what about kibbutzim? An actual socialist-zionist utopia that worked for decades following most communist theoris such as no private property, and yet it slowly turned into a market-based private industry.

As a matter of fact, socialism either turns into a totalitarian dystopia (yeah, including National Socialism or Christianity), or it dissolves. Private property and market, instead, exist at least since the first grain silo and the wall around it was built back in 5,000 B.C. (at least).

It must mean something.

Society, like all things, requires that happy middle ground, that golden ratio. Up or down, groups of people are going to both compete and co-operate. Siblings will fight within the family, but in inter-family squabbles they will back each other up. Likewise, inter-family squabbling is put aside in favour of cohesion when tribes of families are in conflict. And tribes unite when the nation is threatened. And so on.

Communism doesn't work because it takes away competition. No human will be content with pure co-operation, especially not if it is enforced through the threat of violence by the state. Just as no human will be content with pure competition, even enemies in dire circumstances will unite and co-operate against mother nature herself if they find themselves stranded.

A barbaric free-for-all will fail because people are inherently social animals and will form alliances. A communist utopia where everyone shares everything and no one competes for glory, pride, or resources will fail because humans want, even require, conflict for growth. Muscles grow when they are stressed. So do people. A conflict free utopia is a pipe-dream. Conflict will be created, even in sport, if for no other reason than for people to entertain themselves.

People want their own, and the freedom to share it with whom they will, within their tribe. They want that happy middle-ground. Everything in moderation, and all that.

You know what happens if you take a bunch of mice and give them everything they could want without struggle? They either stop moving and simply die, or they turn feral and eat each other. Struggle, conflict, these things are required. A work-free, conflict-free utopia will not breed eternal peace. It will breed a generation of chaos and despair and, perhaps, in that conflict, some number of that generation might find purpose, and through that purpose find peace with their place.
